findings.issue_text: src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — For a detector of registered type `metric_alert_fire`, changing its handler to `StatefulDetectorHandler` without implementing `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, or `build_occurrence_and_event_data` breaks the registry’s instantiable-handler contract: `Detector.detector_handler` raises TypeError instead of returning the previously concrete handler, aborting `process_detectors` before later detectors are processed (confidence 100; severity P2; blocking; code: `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]):`).

src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — Processing a detector registered as metric_alert_fire now raises TypeError at Detector.detector_handler before evaluation because MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits four unimplemented abstract members (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data), aborting processing of that detector and subsequent detectors in the batch (confidence 100; severity P2; blocking; code: `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]):`).

src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — Accessing detector_handler for a metric_alert_fire detector now raises TypeError because the registered MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits four unimplemented abstract members, so callers cannot obtain the previously instantiable handler (confidence 100; severity P2; advisory; code: `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]):`; rebuttal: metric alerts are currently example scaffolding, but the class remains registered as MetricAlertFire.detector_handler and Detector.detector_handler unconditionally instantiates it, so the first caller using that advertised type fails before evaluation instead of receiving the previous empty result).

tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:191 — The new hook's measurement forwarding is unverified because the multi-group packet supplies 10 for group_2 but its expected occurrence supplies 6 and build_mock_occurrence_and_event never reads value, so substituting any measurement in the production hook call leaves these assertions passing while occurrence builders receive incorrect evidence (confidence 100; severity P2; advisory; code: `detector.detector_handler, "group_2", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH`; rebuttal: the fixture need not implement real occurrence formatting, but it must observe the value argument to verify the forwarding contract introduced by this diff, either through an argument assertion or value-dependent output).

tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:206 — The new multi-group publication assertion accepts additional Kafka calls, so publishing group_2 twice still passes and leaves consumers exposed to duplicate occurrences without a failing regression test (confidence 100; severity P3; advisory; code: `mock_produce_occurrence_to_kafka.assert_has_calls(`; rebuttal: the single-group test asserts one call and the result dictionary contains two entries, but neither constrains side effects for a second group, so this test also needs an exact call count or complete call-list comparison).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — Processing a detector registered as metric_alert_fire now raises TypeError at Detector.detector_handler before evaluation because MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits four unimplemented abstract members (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data), aborting processing of that detector and subsequent detectors in the batch (confidence 100; severity P2; blocking; code: `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]):`).

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that MetricAlertDetectorHandler will raise TypeError because it inherits abstract methods without implementing them. However, in Python, a class with unimplemented abstract methods only raises TypeError when you try to instantiate it, not when it's defined. The class is defined with 'pass' which is valid Python - it simply inherits all behavior from StatefulDetectorHandler. The actual issue would only occur at runtime if someone tries to instantiate MetricAlertDetectorHandler directly. Looking at the diff, this is a placeholder class (the TODO comment even says 'This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction'), and the tests use MockDetectorStateHandler which properly implements all abstract methods. The finding incorrectly states this would cause immediate TypeError at class definition time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — Accessing detector_handler for a metric_alert_fire detector now raises TypeError because the registered MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits four unimplemented abstract members, so callers cannot obtain the previously instantiable handler (confidence 100; severity P2; advisory; code: `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]):`; rebuttal: metric alerts are currently example scaffolding, but the class remains registered as MetricAlertFire.detector_handler and Detector.detector_handler unconditionally instantiates it, so the first caller using that advertised type fails before evaluation instead of receiving the previous empty result).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows MetricAlertDetectorHandler changing from inheriting DetectorHandler (with a concrete evaluate method returning []) to inheriting StatefulDetectorHandler (which is abstract). Looking at StatefulDetectorHandler in the diff, it has abstract methods: get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data. The new MetricAlertDetectorHandler only has 'pass' and doesn't implement these abstract methods. When Detector.detector_handler property tries to instantiate this handler via group_type.detector_handler(self), it will fail with TypeError because you cannot instantiate a class with unimplemented abstract methods. This is a real bug - the class was previously functional (returned empty list) but now cannot be instantiated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:206 — The new multi-group publication assertion accepts additional Kafka calls, so publishing group_2 twice still passes and leaves consumers exposed to duplicate occurrences without a failing regression test (confidence 100; severity P3; advisory; code: `mock_produce_occurrence_to_kafka.assert_has_calls(`; rebuttal: the single-group test asserts one call and the result dictionary contains two entries, but neither constrains side effects for a second group, so this test also needs an exact call count or complete call-list comparison).

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test uses `assert_has_calls(..., any_order=True)` which only verifies that the specified calls were made, but doesn't verify that ONLY those calls were made. If `produce_occurrence_to_kafka` were called more times (e.g., duplicates), the test would still pass. However, looking at the diff, the `process_detectors` function now uses a dictionary keyed by `group_key` (line 48-49: `results = {}` and `results[result.group_key] = result`), which inherently prevents duplicate group keys from being processed. The finding is technically correct that the test could be more strict, but the code change actually does prevent duplicates through the dictionary structure. This is a valid test improvement suggestion but not a bug since the code itself handles deduplication.
